description: Welcome to EcoOrbit, a passionate team for the Cumilla NASA Space Apps Challenge taking on the "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA’s Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars" challenge. We combine space exploration, data, and creative storytelling to highlight humanity's footprint on lunar and Martian surfaces. We are looking for collaborative innovators in software, coding, design, storytelling, and space science. Join us to build an impactful project!
summary:
EcoOrbit NASA Space Apps

EcoOrbit is a web platform that turns NASA Earth observation data into clear, actionable environmental insights for communities, students, and local decision-makers. Satellite data is powerful but hard to interpret, so environmental change often goes unnoticed until damage is done. EcoOrbit brings open NASA data, including MODIS vegetation indices, Landsat imagery, GPM rainfall, and FIRMS fire detections, into one interactive dashboard.

Users pick a location and view trends in vegetation health, temperature, rainfall, and wildfire activity. An LLM-powered layer detects anomalies such as deforestation, drought stress, and urban heat growth, explains them in plain language, and gives simple risk scores and early warnings. A storytelling mode with before-and-after views helps students and teachers explore their own region.

EcoOrbit is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interface, Python for data processing and LLM integration, and C, C++, and C# for performance-critical analysis and supporting tools. An antivirus API scans uploaded files and links to keep users safe. The code is managed on GitHub, and YouTube hosts demos and tutorials.

EcoOrbit makes NASA data accessible to everyone, one orbit at a time.

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 | Theme: “The Next Frontier”
Motto: Learn • Explore • Model • Protect-

EcoOrbit NASA Space Apps

Overview

EcoOrbit is an educational space-technology platform about orbital sustainability. It brings satellites, space debris, launch carbon impact and responsible orbital operations together in one browser-based experience. Anyone can use it, including students, kids and curious adults, without specialist software or mission-control experience.

It was built by a six-person team from Bangladesh as an independent participant project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.

The problem

Low Earth orbit is getting crowded. Debris, congestion and the carbon footprint of launches and satellites threaten orbit as a shared resource. Most people never learn how this works, and the existing tools are built for specialists.

Our solution

EcoOrbit turns these ideas into something people can see and try. The experience has three steps:

  1. Observe: explore satellites and debris on an interactive 3D globe with live telemetry.
  2. Understand: use calculators and explainers to connect orbital activity with sustainability and safety.
  3. Imagine: explore green credits and responsible orbital operations as possible future solutions.

Key features

  • Interactive 3D globe and the VLZO UFO Simulator, with a telemetry dashboard.
  • Sustainability Score calculator covering launch footprint, de-orbit planning and debris mitigation.
  • Collision risk alerts, and carbon credit tracking for orbital activity.
  • Omar, an astronaut chatbot and voice guide, plus VLZO TV.
  • Junior Space Explorers Hub and Kids Story for young learners.
  • Cyber security test with a certificate.
  • Membership plans, a members directory and EcoOrbit Meetings for voice and video calls.

Values

  • Education first: clear, friendly explanations for all ages.
  • Sustainability: measuring the footprint of launches, satellites and debris.
  • Accessibility: works in the browser, with a voice guide and astronaut helper.
  • Honesty: every output is labelled as an educational estimate, not real flight guidance.
